question: Suspended solids in water can increase the haziness of the water. Which of the following represents the measurement of haziness of water?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Turbidity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Turbidity** is the measure of the degree to which water loses its transparency due to the presence of suspended particulates.
 
• It is an important indicator of water quality and clarity, with higher turbidity indicating higher levels of suspended solids.
 
• Turbidity is commonly measured in Nephelometric Turbidity Units (NTU).
 
• High turbidity can indicate potential contamination and can affect aquatic life by reducing the amount of light penetrating the water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solubility:**

 
 
• Solubility refers to the ability of a substance to dissolve in a solvent, forming a homogeneous solution at a specified temperature and pressure.
 
• It is typically expressed in terms of the maximum amount of solute that can dissolve in a given amount of solvent.
 
 
 
• **Salinity:**
 
 
• Salinity is the measure of all the salts dissolved in water, usually expressed in parts per thousand (ppt).
 
• It is an important factor in determining the chemical and physical properties of water.
 
 
 
• **Viscosity:**
 
 
• Viscosity is the measure of a fluid's resistance to flow or deformation.
 
• It is an intrinsic property of the fluid and is influenced by temperature and pressure.
